label: conj
title: Conjecture
body_md:
\label{conj}
The (untwisted) Whitehead double of a knot $K$ is slice if and only if $K$ is slice.
head: environment

label: thm: main theorem
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: main theorem}
    Let $W_K$ be the untwisted positive Whitehead double of \(K\subset S^3\). Then zero is a characterising slope for $W_K$.
head: environment

label: thm: main thm gen
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: main thm gen}
Assume $K\subset S^3$ is not a $(p,q)$-torus knot nor a $(p,q)$-cable knot. Then, for each $n\in \ensuremath {\mathbb{Z}}$, zero is a characterising slope for $W^n_{K}$. If $K$ is a $(p,q)$-torus knot or a  $(p,q)$-cable, then the same holds when $n\ne pq$.
head: environment

label: rem: conventions
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem: conventions}
In this paper, we follow the convention that the $(p,q)$-cable of a knot $J$ is the one that lies on the boundary of a tubular neighbourhood of $J$ and winds $p$ times around the canonical longitude of $J$ and $q$ times around the meridian of $J$. Moreover, we will always assume that cables are \emph{non-trivial}, that is to say that the $(p,q)$-cable of a knot $J$ is never an unlink or equal to $J$. Analogously, we will assume that a $(p,q)$-torus knot is not the unknot.
head: environment

title: Corollary
body_md: Zero is a characterising slope for all twist knots.
head: environment

label: thm: band in annulus
title: Theorem
body_md:
\label{thm: band in annulus}
   Let $L_K$ be the $(2,2n)$-cable of a knot $K$, oriented as the boundary of a cabling annulus. Let $\widetilde{K}$ be the knot obtained by an oriented banding of $L_K$ along a band $b$. Then $\widetilde{K}$ is the unknot if and only if $b$ can be isotoped in a cabling annulus for $L_K$.

head: environment

title: Theorem
body_md:
For every compact orientable and irreducible $3$-manifold $M$ there exists a collection of finitely many disjoint incompressible tori 
such that each component formed by cutting along these tori is either atoroidal or a Seifert manifold. Moreover, a minimal such collection is unique up to isotopy.
head: environment
name: JSJ decomposition theorem

label: thm: wald and Hatc
title: Theorem
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
The statement on the uniqueness of the Seifert fibration on $M$ up to isotopy is a direct consequence of \cite[Satz 10.1]{WALDHAUSEN1967}; see also \cite[Theorem VI.18]{jaco1980lectures}.
As a consequence of \cite[Lemma 1.16]{hatcher2007notes}, all essential annuli can be isotoped to be vertical with respect to this Seifert fibration.
head: environment

label: lem: JSJ
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: JSJ}
Let $K\subset S^3$ be a non-trivial knot satisfying Assumption \ref{assum 1}, and let $\mathcal{T}=\{T_1,\dots, T_k\}$ be the JSJ tori of the JSJ decomposition of $E_K$. Then the manifold $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ has a JSJ decomposition given by $\mathcal{T}\cup \{\partial E_K, F\}$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We first prove that all tori in $\mathcal{T}\cup \partial E_K\cup F$ are incompressible in $S^3_0(W_K^n)$, starting with $F$. First recall that \cite[Theorem~3.1]{Gabaifol3} and the fact that $W_K^n$ is a non-trivial knot imply that $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ is irreducible. In particular, since $F$ is non-trivial in the second homology group of $S^3_0(W_K^n)$, it is incompressible, otherwise it would be homologous to a sphere, and hence separating. 

By construction, cutting $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ along $\partial E_K$ yields $E_K\cup S^3_{0,\bullet}(W)$. The torus $\partial E_K$ is incompressible in $E_K$ since $K$ is non-trivial, and incompressible in $S^3_{0,\bullet}(W)$, since a compressing disc, via an innermost argument, can be made disjoint from $F$, and hence would imply the existence of a compressing disc inside $P\times S^1$, which is not possible. This implies that $\partial E_K$ is incompressible in $S^3_0(W_K^n)$.

Regarding the tori in $\mathcal{T}$, if there exists a compressing disc in $S^3_0(W_K^n)$, then by an innermost argument again, we can suppose that it is disjoint from $\partial E_K$. However, this would imply compressibility in $E_K$, which contradicts our hypotheses.

 By construction, cutting $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ along the tori in this collection produces a union of Seifert fibered manifolds and atoroidal manifolds. In order to prove that the collection $\mathcal{T}\cup \{\partial E_K, F\}$ defines a JSJ decomposition, we need to show that this set is minimal.
First of all, notice that $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ is not a torus semi-bundle since its first homology group does not contain any torsion (we refer to \cite{Martelli2016AnIT} for a definition of torus semi-bundles). Moreover, by \cite[Corollary~8.23]{Gabaifol3}, the manifold $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ is a torus bundle if and only if $W_K^n$ is, up to mirror, the trefoil or the figure-eight knot. Since $K$ is a non-trivial knot by hypothesis, we conclude that $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ is not a torus bundle.

Therefore the set of incompressible tori $\mathcal{T} \cup \{\partial E_K , F\}$ is not minimal if and only if, when we cut $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ along them, two adjacent pieces are Seifert fibered and their fibers match up under the gluing (see for example the proof of \cite[Proposition~11.5.4]{Martelli2016AnIT}).
 As a consequence, the tori in $\mathcal{T}$ must be JSJ tori for $S^3_0(W_K^n)$. By Theorem \ref{thm: wald and Hatc},
 the manifold $P \times S^1$ has a unique Seifert fibration up to isotopy, and its fibers are $\{x\} \times S^1$, $x \in P$. Since the fibers are not preserved by the gluing map in Lemma \ref{lem: gluing map}, it follows that $S^3_{0,\bullet}(W)$ is not Seifert fibered. Therefore, $F$ is a JSJ torus for $S^3_0(W_K^n).$

 We are left with checking that $\partial E_K$ is a JSJ torus.
Of course, if the outermost piece $N$ of the JSJ decomposition of $E_K$ is not Seifert fibered then $\partial E_K$ is a JSJ torus.
We therefore just need to check the case where $N$ is Seifert fibered. In that case, by \cite{Budney2005JSJdecompositionsOK} (see also \cite[Theorem 2.6]{Wak}), there are three possibilities:
\begin{itemize}
\item $K$ is the $(p,q)$-torus knot;
\item $K$ is the $(p,q)$-cable of a non-trivial knot $J$;
\item $K$ is a composite knot.
\end{itemize}
In the first and second case, since $K$ is non-trivial, $N$ has a unique Seifert fibration and its regular fibers have slope $pq \neq 0$ on $\partial E_K$. 
Lastly, if $K$ is composite, the regular fibers of the outermost piece have meridional slope on $\partial E_K$. 

Recall that the boundary component of $P\times S^1$ identified to $\partial E_K$ corresponds to the boundary of a tubular neighbourhood of one of the two components of the Whitehead link, and by the definition of fibered link given in Section \ref{sec: lemmas}, the regular fibers $\{pt\}\times S^1$ corresponds to meridians of this component. Since we are considering the $n$-twisted Whitehead double of $K$, the gluing map identifies these meridians to the $n$-longitudes of $K$, and since $K$ satisfies Assumption \ref{assum 1}, they are not identified to the regular fibers of $N$. This proves that $\partial E_K$ is a JSJ torus of $S^3_0(W_K^n)$.
head: environment

label: lem: JSJ banale
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: JSJ banale}
Let $n\neq -1, 0, 1$ and $K\subset S^3$ be the unknot. Then $F$ is the unique JSJ torus of $S^3_0(W_K^n)$, and the unique JSJ piece is Seifert fibered and atoroidal.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
First notice that also in this case $S^3_0(W^n_K)$ is irreducible and $F$ is incompressible. 
 Cutting $S^3_0(W^n_K)$ along $F \cup \partial E_K$ yields the disjoint union of $E_K$ and $P \times S^1$, and the fibers of the Seifert fibration of $P\times S^1$ are identified with simple closed curves of slope $n$ in $\partial E_K$.


 Since $E_K$ is a solid torus, it admits a Seifert fibration with fibers of slope $ {n}$ on $\partial E_K$. This shows that $S^3_0(W^n_K)$ cut along $F$ is a Seifert fibered space over the annulus with one exceptional fiber of order $|n|$, and in particular is atoroidal. 
 
 
 
 If this manifold is not $S^1 \times S^1 \times I$, this Seifert fibration is unique up to isotopy (see Theorem \ref{thm: wald and Hatc}). 
 The manifold $S^1\times S^1 \times I$ admits only one Seifert fibration up to diffeomorphism \cite[Theorem 2.3]{hatcher2007notes}, and has no exceptional fibers. Hence, if $n\neq \pm 1$, $S^3_0(W^n_K)$ cut along $F$ is not $S^1 \times S^1 \times I$.
 Moreover, since $n \neq \pm 1$, the manifold $S^3_0(W^n_K)$ is not a torus (semi-)bundle (see the proof of Lemma \ref{lem: JSJ}), and therefore the same argument as in the proof of Lemma \ref{lem: JSJ} allows us to show that $F$ is a JSJ torus.
head: environment

label: lem: F unique
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: F unique}
    If $S$ is an incompressible, non-separating torus in $S^3_0(W_K^n)$, then $S$ is isotopic to $F$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We start by showing that $S$ can be assumed to be disjoint from the JSJ tori of $S^3_0(W^n_K)$. The argument follows essentially the proof of uniqueness of the JSJ decomposition.


Recall that by Lemma \ref{lem: JSJ} and Lemma \ref{lem: JSJ banale} we know the JSJ decomposition of $S^3_0(W^n_K)$.
After performing an isotopy, we can suppose that $S$ is transverse to all the JSJ tori                                                
and that the intersection of $S$ with the JSJ tori has a minimal number of connected components. We assume that this number is positive, since otherwise $S$ is already disjoint from the JSJ tori.
Since the JSJ pieces are irreducible and the JSJ tori are incompressible, we can suppose that $S$ is cut by the JSJ tori into annuli, and that each of these annuli is essential in its JSJ piece. The atoroidal pieces that contain essential annuli are Seifert fibered (see \cite[Lemma 1.18]{hatcher2007notes}), and hence $S$ must intersect only Seifert fibered JSJ pieces. As a consequence of Theorem \ref{thm: wald and Hatc} and our hypotheses, the Seifert fibered JSJ pieces of $S^3_0(W_K^n)$ all admit a unique Seifert fibration up to isotopy, and essential annuli can be isotoped to be vertical in their Seifert fibered pieces. This means that if $T$ is a JSJ torus with $T \cap S \neq \emptyset$, then the Seifert fibrations on the Seifert pieces containing $T$ match along $T$. But this would lead to a contradiction, since in that case $T$ could be removed from the JSJ tori.

Therefore we can suppose that $S$ is disjoint from the JSJ tori, and hence contained in one of the JSJ pieces. 
If $K$ is the unknot, by Assumption \ref{assum 1} we know that $n \neq 0,1,-1$, and that by Lemma \ref{lem: JSJ banale} the unique JSJ piece is Seifert fibered and atoroidal. Since $S$ is incompressible in $S^3_0(W^n_K)$, we deduce that it is isotopic to $F$. 

We will therefore suppose that $K$ is non-trivial.
Since every torus in $S^3$ is separating and $S$ is not, $S$ cannot be contained in $E_K\subset S^3$, meaning that $S$ must be contained in the JSJ piece $P \times S^1$. Up to isotopy, the torus $S$ is vertical in $P \times S^1 $ (see \cite[Proposition 1.12]{hatcher2007notes}), and hence isotopic to one of its boundary components. In $S^3_0 (W_K^n)$ the boundary components of $P \times S^1$ get sent to $\partial E_K$ and $F$. Again, since $S$ is not separating, it cannot be isotopic to $\partial E_K$, and so it must be isotopic to $F$.
head: environment

label: lem: fig8 and trefoil
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: fig8 and trefoil}
Assume that $K$ is the unknot and that $n=\pm 1$. If $S$ is an incompressible, non-separating torus in $S^3_0(W^n_K)$, then $S$ is isotopic to $F$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
In this case, $W^n_K$ is the trefoil or the figure-eight knot, and its $0$-surgery fibers over the circle, with $F$ as a fiber. Every non-separating torus in $S^3_0(W^n_K)$ has a dual curve, and therefore it is a generator of
the second homology group. In particular, it must be homologous, and hence isotopic to $F$ (see, e.g. \cite[Chapter 1.4]{EisNeu}).
head: environment

label: prop: Sigma cap to F
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: Sigma cap to F}
Let $K$ and $K'$ be knots in $S^3$ satisfying Assumption \ref{assum 1}. Then the $3$-genus of $K'$ is one, and if $\Sigma$ is a Seifert surface of genus one for $K'$, the diffeomorphism $S^3_0(K') \cong S^3_0(W_K^n)$ sends the capped Seifert surface $ \widehat{\Sigma}$ to a surface isotopic to $F$. The same holds if $W_K^n$ is the trefoil or the figure-eight knot.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\Sigma$ be a minimal genus Seifert surface for $K'$.
As consequence of \cite[Theorem~3.1]{Gabaifol3}, the surface $\widehat{\Sigma} $ has minimal genus among the surfaces representing a generator of $H_2(S^3_0(K');\ensuremath {\mathbb{Z}}) \cong \ensuremath {\mathbb{Z}}$. In particular, $\widehat{\Sigma}$ is incompressible in $S^3_0(K')$, and if two knots have diffeomorphic $0$-surgeries, then they have the same $3$-genus. Since the $n$-twisted Whitehead double of a knot has genus one whenever $n \neq 0$ or $K$ is non-trivial, we deduce that $K'$ has genus one. This implies that $\widehat{\Sigma}$ is an incompressible torus in $S^3_{0}(K')$, and by Lemma \ref{lem: F unique}, or Lemma \ref{lem: fig8 and trefoil} in the case of the trefoil or the figure-eight knot,  the diffeomorphism $S^3_0(K') \cong S^3_0(W_K^n)$ maps it to a surface isotopic to $F$.
head: environment

label: defn: banding
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{defn: banding}
Let $L$ be a link in $S^3$, and let $b$ be an embedding of $I\times I$ into $S^3$ with $b(I\times I)\cap L=b(I\times \partial I)$. The link $L'=\left(L\setminus b(I\times \partial I)\right)\cup b(\partial I\times I)$ is called a \emph{banding} of $L$. If $L$ is oriented, an \emph{oriented banding} of $L$ is a banding that respects the orientations of the components of $L$.
head: environment

title: Remark
body_md: Note that if the link $L$ is a split link with two components, and the band intersects both components, then a banding of $L$ corresponds to a band sum of the components of $L$.
head: environment

label: lem: unique annulus
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: unique annulus}
Let $L_K$ be the $(2,2n)$-cable of a knot $K$, and assume that $L_K$ is not the Hopf link. If $K$ is the $(p,q)$-torus knot or the $(p,q)$-cable of a non-trivial knot $J$, further assume that $n\ne pq$. Then, there exists a unique incompressible annulus $A$ in $E_{L_K}$, and it is a cabling annulus. If $L_K$ is the Hopf link, then there exist exactly two incompressible annuli $A_1$ and $A_2$ in $E_{L_K}$ with the property that $\partial A_i = L_{K}$, and they are cabling annuli.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
If $K$ is non-trivial, arguing as in the proof of Lemma~\ref{lem: JSJ}, one shows that the JSJ decomposition of $E_{L_K}$ has as outermost piece $P \times S^1$. The annulus $A$ must be vertical in $P \times S^1$ and therefore it coincides with the unique cabling annulus $c \times S^1$, where $c$ is an arc in $P$ connecting the two boundary components $\partial_0$ and $\partial_1$. Clearly, cutting $E_{L_K}$ along $A$ yields $E_K$.  Suppose now that $K$ is trivial and $n \neq \pm 1$. The manifold $E_{L_K}$ admits a Seifert fibering over the annulus with one exceptional fiber of order $|n|$ and $A$ must be vertical by Theorem \ref{thm: wald and Hatc}. Since all vertical annuli in $E_{L_K}$ are isotopic, we conclude.

We now consider the case of $K$ trivial and $n=\pm 1$, i.e. when $L_K$ is the Hopf link. In this case, $E_{L_K}\cong T\times I$, and by \cite[Lemma 1.16]{hatcher2007notes}, every essential annulus can be made vertical, up to changing the Seifert fibration. Since every Seifert fibration of $T\times I$ is given by crossing a fibration in circles of $T$ with $I$, this implies that there are at most two non-isotopic essential annuli in $E_{L_K}$ with the required boundary: those with slope $+1$ and $-1$ respectively. Since they have different slopes on the boundary, they are not isotopic.
head: environment

label: lem: every annulus is cabling
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: every annulus is cabling}
    Let $L_K$ be the $(2,2n)$-cable of a knot $K$. Let $A$ be an incompressible annulus in $E_{L_K}$ with $\partial A=L_K$. Then $A$ is a cabling annulus for $L_K$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: By Lemma \ref{lem: unique annulus} we only need to consider the case of $K$ being the $(p,q)$-torus knot or the $(p,q)$-cable of a non-trivial knot $J$ and $n=pq$. In the first case, $L_K$ is the $(2p,2q)$ torus link and $E_{L_K}$ is a Seifert fibered space over the annulus with two exceptional fibers of order $|p|$ and $|q|$. In the second case, the outermost piece of the JSJ decomposition of $E_{L_K}$ is Seifert fibered with one exceptional fiber of order $|q|$. In both cases there are many isotopy classes of annuli intersecting both components of $\partial E_{L_K}$. However, by using Theorem \ref{thm: wald and Hatc} as in the previous proof, one sees that  these annuli must all be vertical, and that cutting $E_{L_K}$ along any of them always yields $E_K$.
head: environment

label: lem: surfaces in solid torus
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem: surfaces in solid torus}
Let $S$ be a genus one surface properly embedded in $S^1\times D^2$ such that $\partial S$ is equal to a meridian. Then $\partial S$ bounds a disc in $S^1\times D^2$ intersecting $S$ only in its boundary.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $D$ be a meridional disc of $S^1 \times D^2$. We can suppose that $D$ and $S$ are transverse, and that the number of connected components of their intersection is minimal. If $D$ and $S$ are disjoint, then $\partial D$ and $\partial S$ co-bound an annulus $A \subseteq \partial (S^1 \times D^2$), and $A \cup D$ is a disc whose intersection with $S$ is $\partial S$.

If $D$ and $S$ are not disjoint, then take a component $C \subseteq D \cap S$ that is innermost in $D$, and let $\Delta$ be the disc in $D$ bounded by $C$. 
Since the intersection between $S$ and $D$ is minimal, cutting $S$ along $D$ yields either a connected surface, or an annulus and a genus one surface. In the first case we can use two parallel copies of $\Delta $ to cap off the cut surface, while in the second case we can use $\Delta$ to cap off the annulus. Both procedures produce a disc. By slightly perturbing the disc, we can make it disjoint from the interior of $S$.
head: environment

title: Proof

body_md:
\label{lem: glue NSigma back}
   The manifold $S^3_0(K')$ is diffeomorphic to the manifold obtained from $E_{L_K}$ by identifying $\widehat{\Sigma}_0$  to $\widehat{\Sigma}_1 $ via $\widehat{\varphi}$.

title: Proof

label: prop: MSigma handlebody
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: MSigma handlebody}
    The manifold $M_\Sigma$ is diffeomorphic to the closure $\overline{S^3 \setminus H_{\alpha}}$ of $S^3 \setminus H_{\alpha}$. This diffeomorphism sends a canonical longitude of $K'$ in $ M_\Sigma$ into a meridian of $\alpha$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The manifold $M_{\Sigma}$ is obtained by cutting $E_{K'}$ along the Seifert surface $\Sigma$. Recall that $E_{K'}$ is diffeomorphic to the exterior of the dual curve $\gamma$ in $ S^3_0(K')$, with a diffeomorphism that identifies the meridian of $\gamma$ to the canonical longitude of $K'$. In other words, removing a tubular neighbourhood of $\gamma \cup \widehat{\Sigma}$ from $S^3_0(K')$ yields $M_\Sigma$, and therefore $M_\Sigma$ is diffeomorphic to the manifold obtained by removing from $N_{\widehat{\Sigma}}$ a tubular neighbourhood of the dual arc $\alpha$, and this, by Lemma  \ref{lem: cutting is cable}, is exactly $\overline{S^3 \setminus H_{\alpha}}$. This concludes the proof, since cutting along $\widehat{\Sigma}$ sends a meridian of $\gamma$ to a meridian of $\alpha$.
head: environment

label: prop: gluing handlebody gives S3
title: Proposition
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We identify $M_{\Sigma}$ with $E_{K'}\setminus \big{(}\Sigma\times(0,1)\big{)}$. By Lemma \ref{lem: glue NSigma back}, we can assume that, for $i=0,1$, the diffeomorphism $\theta$ between $M_{\Sigma}$ and $\overline{S^3 \setminus H_{\alpha}}$ given by Proposition~\ref{prop: MSigma handlebody} maps $\Sigma\times \{i\}\subset \partial M_{\Sigma}$ to $\Sigma_i$ and satisfies $\theta(s,1)=\varphi \circ \theta(s,0)$ for all $s\in \Sigma$. 


We identify $\Sigma\times [0,1]$ with $\Sigma_0\times [0,1]$ via the map $\theta_{|\Sigma\times \{0\}}\times \rm id$, and $M_{\Sigma}$ with $\overline{S^3 \setminus H_{\alpha}}$ via $\theta$. 
Gluing $M_\Sigma$ to $\Sigma\times [0,1]$ along $\operatorname{{id}}_{\Sigma \times \{0\}} \sqcup \operatorname{{id}}_{\Sigma \times \{1\}}$ produces $E_{K'}$, and this gluing can be extended to the whole boundary of $\Sigma \times [0,1]$ to produce $S^3$.
If we take the corresponding gluing between $\Sigma_0\times [0,1]$ and $\overline{S^3 \setminus H_{\alpha}}$ via the above identifications, we obtain the desired result.
head: environment

label: prop: Ktilde
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: Ktilde}
The manifold obtained by gluing a neighbourhood of the compressing disc $D_m$ to $\overline{S^3 \setminus H_{\alpha}}$  along the restriction of $\widetilde{\psi}$ is the exterior of a knot $\widetilde{K}\subset S^3$. Moreover $\widetilde{K}$ is a banding of $L_K$ along a band whose core is the dual arc $\alpha$.
head: environment

title: Proof
head: environment

label: rmk: banding unoriented
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rmk: banding unoriented}
Recall that we oriented $L_K$ so that its components are parallel. With respect to this orientation, the banding from Proposition \ref{prop: Ktilde} is not oriented. However, if we change the orientation of one of the components, then it becomes an oriented banding. Notice that, with this orientation, $L_K$ is the boundary of a cabling annulus.
head: environment

label: prop: Ktilde is unknot
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop: Ktilde is unknot}
    The manifold obtained by $+1$ surgery on $\widetilde{K}$ is diffeomorphic to $S^3$, via a diffeomorphism that maps the meridian of $\alpha$ to $K'$. In particular $\widetilde{K}$ is the unknot.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
By Propositions \ref{prop: gluing handlebody gives S3} and \ref{prop: Ktilde}, gluing a solid torus to the exterior of $\widetilde{K}$ along the slope defined by $\widetilde{\psi}(\partial D_l)$ gives $S^3$. 
By Proposition \ref{prop: MSigma handlebody} this diffeomorphism sends the meridian of $\alpha$ to $K'$.
Since ${\psi}(l_{K_0})= m_{K_1} + l_{K_1}$, where we are adopting the same orientation conventions of Proposition \ref{prop: Ktilde}, we have that $\widetilde{\psi}(\partial D_l)$ is equal to 
$$ \overset{\circ}{l}_{K_0} \cup k_1 \cup k_2 \cup -\overset{\circ} {(m_{K_1}+ l_{K_1})}$$
where $k_1$ and $k_2$ are disjoint properly embedded arcs in the boundary of the tubular neighbourhood of $\alpha$ parallel to $j_1$ and $j_2$. 
Here \(\overset{\circ}{(m_{K_1}+ l_{K_1})} \) indicates the properly embedded oriented arc in $\Sigma_1$ corresponding to the oriented simple closed curve representing $m_{K_1}+ l_{K_1}$. Clearly the simple closed curve $\widetilde{\psi}(\partial D_l)$ is a longitude of $\widetilde{K}$ and therefore defines an integer framing of it, which we now determine. 

First, we orient $\widetilde{K}$ by extending the orientation of $K_0$ (equivalently, by extending the orientation of  $-K_1$).
Note that the curve $\widetilde{\psi}(\partial D_l)$ is homologous to $l_{K_0}-(m_{K_1}+l_{K_1})$ in $\overline{S^3\setminus H_\alpha}$. The inclusion of $\overline{S^3\setminus H_\alpha}$ into $E_{L_K}$ induces an isomorphism on the first homology groups, and, since $l_{K_0}$ and $l_{K_1}$ are isotopic in $E_{L_K}$, one has the equality $l_{K_0}-(m_{K_1}+l_{K_1})= -m_{K_1}$ in $H_1(\overline{S^3\setminus H_\alpha})$. Since $-m_{K_1}$ is a positive meridian for $-K_1$, its image in $E_{\widetilde{K}}$ is a positive meridian of $\widetilde{K}$.
As a consequence of \cite{GorLue}, $\widetilde{K}$ must be the unknot.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md:
We start by noting that if $K$ is the unknot and $n=0$, then $W^n_K$ is the unknot, and the result follows from \cite[Corollary~8.3]{Gabaifol3}.

We can now assume that $K$ and $K'$ satisfy Assumption \ref{assum 2}.
In this case, by Proposition~\ref{prop: Ktilde is unknot} we know that $K'$ is the image of the meridian of the band $b$ in the $1$-surgery on $\widetilde{K}$, where $\widetilde{K}$ is the result of a banding of  the $(2,2n)$-cable $L_K$ of $K$ along the band $b$. By Remark~\ref{rmk: banding unoriented}, this is an oriented banding with respect to the orientation on $L_K$ induced by a cabling annulus. Hence, Theorem~\ref{thm: band in annulus} implies that the band $b$ can be isotoped in a cabling annulus $A$ in the exterior of $L_K$, and so we are in the situation described in Figure~\ref{fig: bing double}. Since the two components of the link in figure can be exchanged with an isotopy, we conclude that $K'$ is isotopic to $W_K^n$.
